prompt:
Image 1 is the target art style. Image 2 is a strip of the scroll 清明上河图 (Along the River During the Qingming Festival) and the only source for what this panel shows. Paint one very wide panel of a painted backdrop in exactly image 1's painting style (hand-inked dark-brown outlines, light hatching, flat muted painted colours, clean readable shapes), showing what image 2 paints, but as a view seen at eye level by a person standing on the ground at the edge of our scene and looking out: looking east along the outer road past the official hall at the end of our scene: the rest of this stretch of the scroll (image 2), seen from its west end at eye level. Image 2's left end is nearest to us and its right end farthest away; its top edge is on our left and its bottom edge on our right. The road runs away from us to the horizon. On it, small and far off: two big two-wheeled family carts with high domed hoods of shaggy brown palm fibre on tall spoked wheels, the far one drawn by two oxen, with drivers, a rider and a few walkers. On the left of the road, nearest: a long hall on a raised floor with a dark blue cloth hanging along its eave, and in front of it a crowd of men standing round a seated man; a wheelwright bent over a big cart wheel; three pack donkeys going up a lane; then a huge, gnarled old tree, bare, with a thick mottled trunk and crooked branches (no leaves and no hanging willow strands), over low mat-awning sheds and an open-fronted tea house with tables and benches; far off on the left, at the end of the road, a bank path with a few tiny porters and four or five big cargo boats with arched mat roofs moored side by side against the bank, only a short reach of deep blue-green water drawn with fine ink ripple lines showing round them, the rest hidden behind low houses and bare trees. On the right of the road: the long grey tiled roofs of big halls one behind another, with a few bare trees.

Rules for the panel:
- Only what image 2 paints. Add nothing that image 2 does not show: no hills or mountains, no distant tree lines or forests, no lakes, rivers or islands, no towers, pagodas, city walls, flags, clouds, birds, sun or haze banks, unless the description above names them. Leave out image 2's red seals, inscriptions and silk damage.
- Eye level. The viewer's eye is at the height of a standing person's eyes, so the horizon is one straight, level line across the whole image, a quarter of the way up from the bottom edge. The heads of all standing people are on that line, near or far; buildings, trees, carts and animals rise above it with their feet just under it. Below the horizon there is only a thin strip of level ground, a tenth of the image height at most. We never look down onto roofs, courtyards or the surface of a road: a road running away from us is a thin wedge of ground narrowing to the horizon. Everything in this picture is far away: its nearest things stand some seventy paces from us, so even the nearest people are small, about a twentieth of the image height, with their heads on the horizon and their feet just under it. The painted ground under the horizon is no deeper than those people are tall, and the road is a flat sliver of it, already narrow at its near end, never a wide wedge opening toward the bottom of the image. Below that sliver of ground there is only white mist.
- Plain white everywhere else. The sky is flat pure white from the top edge down to the horizon, behind everything: no clouds, no blue, no gradient, no haze, no texture, no paper grain. Below the strip of ground the bottom of the image is the same pure white: the ground ends in soft white mist. The upper part of the image, above the tallest trees and roofs, is empty white.
- Clear and crisp: every outline and colour as clear as in image 1, with no atmospheric haze and no fading toward the distance (the world adds its own mist). Trees keep clear branches and twigs with white showing between them.
- The left and right eighths of the image hold only low ground and a few small things; they will fade into mist.
- Colours of the real town in soft spring daylight, as in image 1: grey-blue clay tiles, white lime plaster, weathered brown timber, tan rammed earth and dusty roads, pale fresh-green willows, dark green pines, bare ink-brown branches. Not the yellow-brown of the aged silk in image 2; no paper texture, no border, no frame, no seal, no text, no signature.
